question: X - band synthetic aperture radar has been used in which satellite?
solution:
The correct answer is __**RISAT-2B**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• RISAT-2B is a radar imaging earth observation satellite developed by ISRO.
 
• It uses X-band synthetic aperture radar (SAR) which allows it to capture high-resolution images regardless of weather conditions.
 
• RISAT-2B was launched on May 22, 2019, from the Sriharikota Range.
 
• The satellite enhances India's capability in applications such as agriculture, forestry, and disaster management support.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **X-band Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR)**

 
 
• SAR is a form of radar that is used to create two-dimensional images or three-dimensional reconstructions of objects, such as landscapes.
 
• X-band refers to the frequency range of the radar waves, which is typically between 8 to 12 GHz.
 
• X-band SAR is known for its high resolution and is commonly used in earth observation satellites.
 
• This technology allows the satellite to capture images in all weather conditions, during day and night.
 
 
 
• **RISAT-2B**
 
 
• RISAT stands for Radar Imaging Satellite.
 
• It is part of India's RISAT series of satellites, which are used for reconnaissance and earth observation.
 
• RISAT-2B provides all-weather surveillance using its X-band SAR payload.
 
• Its primary applications include monitoring agriculture, forestry, soil moisture, and disaster management.
 
 
 
• **ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation)**
 
 
• ISRO is the space agency of the Government of India, headquartered in Bengaluru.
 
• It is responsible for advancing space technology and using its applications for various national tasks.
 
• ISRO has successfully launched numerous satellites into space, including communication, earth observation, and interplanetary missions.
 
• Notable missions include the Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan) and the Chandrayaan missions to the moon.
